body:
### Describe the bug

After upgrading to 3.3.0, I've started getting crashes with some compiled python code.

After compiling with debug symbols, I find that the crash is centred on the following C code:

```c
  /* "lib/foo.py":242
 *             <snip>
 *
 *         part = offset = 0             # <<<<<<<<<<<<<<
 *         <snip>
 *         <snip>
*/
  __Pyx_INCREF(__pyx_mstate_global->__pyx_int_0);
  __Pyx_XDECREF_SET(__pyx_v_part, __pyx_mstate_global->__pyx_int_0);

  __pyx_v_offset = ((PyObject*)0);
```

which then gets used later on, and predictably, crashes horribly

### Code to reproduce the behaviour:

Minimal reproducer:

```cython
def do_stuff():
    mapping: dict[int, int] = {}
    for line_number, _content in enumerate([]):
        part = line_number

    part = offset = 0

    for address in range(0, 1):
        if line_number := mapping.get(address):
            part = line_number
            offset = part
            print(offset)
```

```shell
uv run cython -o test.c test.py
```

And have a look at the generated c code.

(and obviously if you were to attempt to run this, it would segfault due to the null dereference)


### Expected behaviour

Code should work as expected and not try to dereference a null object. Further reductions get the expected

```c
  __Pyx_INCREF(__pyx_mstate_global->__pyx_int_0);
  __Pyx_XDECREF_SET(__pyx_v_part, __pyx_mstate_global->__pyx_int_0);
  __Pyx_INCREF(__pyx_mstate_global->__pyx_int_0);
  __pyx_v_offset = __pyx_mstate_global->__pyx_int_0;
```

or

```c
  __Pyx_INCREF(__pyx_mstate_global->__pyx_int_0);
  __Pyx_XDECREF_SET(__pyx_v_part, __pyx_mstate_global->__pyx_int_0);
  __pyx_v_offset = 0;
```

apparently depending on how the type resolver manages things

So possibly there's some confusion going on about what to do when the type is determined when not?

### OS

Linux & Windows

### Python version

3.14.4

### Cython version

3.3.0

### Additional context

_No response_
title: [BUG] Null dereference with multiple assignments in single statement
